question: In Figure 2A-2, what minimum mounting height and lateral offset are shown for a basic roadside sign in a rural area without a wider shoulder?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 2A-2, Panel A ("Roadside sign in rural area") shows a minimum mounting height of 5 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement, and a minimum lateral offset of 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way. The 6-foot offset from the edge of the shoulder (Panel B) applies only where a shoulder wider than 6 feet exists. Standards (mandatory): - "In rural areas, the minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement, of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 5 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." Guidance (recommended): - "For post-mounted signs, the minimum lateral offset should be 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way. If a shoulder wider than 6 feet exists, the minimum lateral offset for post-mounted signs should be 6 feet from the edge of the shoulder." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2A-2, Panel A depicts a STOP sign in a rural area with "5 ft MIN." vertical height from the bottom of the sign to the near pavement edge elevation and "12 ft MIN." lateral offset from the traveled way, while Panel B shows the alternate "6 ft MIN." offset case labeled "Shoulder wider than 6 ft." [Image 2] The full-page view of Figure 2A-2 confirms the same 5 ft MIN. height and 12 ft MIN. offset dimensions for Panel A. [Image 5] Figure 2A-3's note reinforces that lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet from the edge of the shoulder or 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way. [Image 3] and [Image 4] show analogous height/offset illustrations for recreational-area and temporary traffic control signs, not the basic rural case in Figure 2A-2. Citations: - Section 2A.15 Standard §4 (p.58) - Section 2A.16 Guidance §3 (p.60) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Page 92 - Page 93
gold_answer: A 5-foot minimum mounting height and a 12-foot minimum lateral offset from the edge of the traveled way.
